extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard contract administrators, procurement analysts, and policy researchers studying A-76 commercial activity contracting
extracted.subtask_description: Assessment and analysis of contracted commercial activities (food service, housing maintenance, security) performed under OMB Circular A-76 for the US Coast Guard, focusing on cost changes, contract administration, performance, and selection of cases for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR responsibilities and expected role
rubrics_metrics.description: The COTR is supposed to be the eyes and ears of the Contracting Officer and should make recommendations to the Contracting Officer concerning contract conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a past Housing Officer directed a COTR not to make recommendations — an improper practice. Effective COTR performance implies active identification and escalation of contract issues to the Contracting Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of contract specialist communications/oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary reliance on letter and telephone correspondence for communications and feedback can lead to failure to notice minor and potentially major problems at the unit level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract specialists should use more direct/robust oversight and not rely solely on written/telephone exchanges; lack of direct engagement can mask problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award approval threshold (COMDT (G-CCS) review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts greater than one million dollars require Chief of Staff (COMDT (G-CCS)) review and approval before award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New expanded contract pending award approval by COMDT (G-CCS) because base year value approaches threshold; follow required internal approval procedures for high-value awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract line-item structure enabling cost tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing housing maintenance costs as separate line items can affect the ability to track cost increases and measure cost-effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although line items exist, the report notes that separation may still make it difficult to measure cost effectiveness; contract structure should support transparent tracking of cost drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of contract cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost increases commonly arise from Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations carried into option years and from negotiated contract extensions or settlements compensating for missed wage increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables (e.g., Table IV) summarize wage increases per option year; analysts should attribute cost changes to wage determinations, negotiated settlements, and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deobligation practice and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A deobligation occurs when actual costs of performance are below the original estimated cost; excess obligated funds are transferred to other accounts or contingencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In food service contracts, declining meal sales caused deobligations which offset wage-driven cost increases; monitor actual volumes against estimates to identify deobligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meal-pricing bands in fixed-price food service contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Each meal type is priced based on ranges of the number of meals sold each month, with higher per-meal prices for lower volumes and lower per-meal prices for higher volumes to cover contractor costs under fixed-price arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If meal sales fall into a lower-volume (higher-price) band but actual customer counts are below the lowest range, the contractor may receive less than originally obligated, triggering deobligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Manager experience and continuity as performance factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor's Project Manager (PM) experience and continuity (e.g., retained PM across contract transitions) are major reasons for contract success and high-quality service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a retired USCG Master Chief retained as PM provided continuity and expertise that contributed to an effectively 'invisible' transition and high satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance measurement via deductions for unsatisfactory performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractor performance is evaluated in part by deductions taken for unsatisfactory performance; absence of deductions is considered evidence of satisfactory/very satisfactory performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: No deductions for unsatisfactory performance were taken on some contracts; one deduction of $446 was recorded for 14 minor discrepancies — record and verify such deductions in contract files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy and relevance of COTR training and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: COTR effectiveness depends on relevant training and prior experience; training that is not well-aligned to duties may not be helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a COTR attended Navy QA training but felt it did not help in COTR duties; newly assigned COTRs requested MLCPAC training or debriefing from prior COTRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of contract specifications to prevent scope disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguous specifications allow contractors to claim additional work outside the intended scope and to negotiate higher prices for tasks that should be within the original scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'exercise meals' were treated as outside-scope leading to additional negotiated payments; specifications should be drafted clearly to limit scope creep and unexpected cost adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of contract documentation and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts with little documentation or based on verbal/handshake agreements hinder proper administration and require subsequent 'patching-up' by contract specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When administration moves (e.g., from D17 to MLCPAC), missing documentation causes difficulties; maintain complete contract records to facilitate oversight and modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications driven by funding availability and continuing resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many contract modifications are required due to limited government funds or Congressional continuing resolutions affecting fund availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables show multiple mods labeled as 'Limited Government funds available' or due to continuing resolutions; plan for funding uncertainty in contract management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of economic indices and price adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts may include adjustments tied to indices such as the Consumer Foods Price Index or specified economic price adjustments for food which affect contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Mod 13 included a 5% Consumer Foods Price Index adjustment; include and track index-based adjustments in cost forecasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor financial stability as a selection/evaluation criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: The contractor's financial condition (e.g., Chapter 11 bankruptcy, unpaid bills to IRS) is a risk to contract continuity and service delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: contractor's Chapter 11 filing led to payments directed to IRS and limited commissary purchasing; assess financial health when awarding and monitoring contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand/customer-base changes impacting contract costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in the customer base or demand (e.g., declining meal sales, deletion of billets due to other contract awards) directly affect revenues, deobligations, and future pricing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: award of BOSS contract deleted 96 civilian and 105 military billets, reducing dining facility customers; monitor demand trends to adjust estimates and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation and contractual treatment of future requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential future requirements (e.g., guards carrying firearms) should be contemplated and addressed in the new contract because they will increase costs if incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support Center Seattle considered future firearm requirement; including such contingencies in the PWS or options helps estimate long-term costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts included in the study: Pacific Area
rubrics_metrics.description: Select Pacific Area contracts to observe the same contract administration as in the previously studied contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures comparability of administrative practices across the sample; selection prioritized geographic/administrative consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts included in the study: Similar complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose contracts similar in complexity to those in the previous study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains methodological consistency by comparing like-with-like in terms of contract complexity and operational scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts included in the study: Deleted billets focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose contracts that had deleted billets of the rate most severely affected by A-76 (Subsistence Specialists (SS)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets contracts where A-76's workforce impacts are most pronounced, enabling study of personnel deletion effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts included in the study: high-cost areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Select commercial activities in high cost areas that may be difficult to support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes remote or logistics-challenged sites (e.g., Kodiak) to observe unique cost drivers and supportability issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for contracts included in the study: maturity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both mature (completed) and current (ongoing) contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of both historical outcomes and current operational performance to identify trends and longer-term effects.
